questions.prompt: A least-squares fit is run on 100 pairs; 3 targets are displaced by 2 m. What best reduces the damage?
options: Increase the voxel size so that the outliers are averaged away.
Run many more iterations of plain least squares until it converges.
Use a trimmed or Huber-loss fit so large residuals get little weight.
Rescale all points to the unit cube before fitting the transform.
questions.explanation: Robust losses or trimming limit the influence of large residuals; more iterations of the same loss converge to the same compromised answer.

questions.prompt: In a translation-only fit using the mean offset, 20 pairs are exact except one displaced by 4 m along x. By how many metres is the estimated translation off?
A mapping run uses 0.1 m voxels. Points (-0.04,0.0) and (0.04,0.0) are given. How many occupied voxels exist when indices use floor? Give the integer.
questions.explanation: floor(-0.4)=-1 and floor(0.4)=0: different cells. Using int() would give 1.

questions.prompt: Neighbourhood covariance has eigenvalues 9, 1 (2D). Compute the surface variation lambda_min/(sum), 2 decimals.
A scan of a smooth sphere is registered with ICP. What is the central difficulty?
options: A sphere has no centroid, so the two point sets cannot be centred before the fit.
Voxel grids cannot represent spheres, so the cloud cannot be downsampled before matching.
ICP cannot handle any curved surface, because the surface normals vary across the cloud.
Rotation about the sphere centre is unconstrained by geometry, so the pose is not unique.
questions.explanation: A sphere is rotationally symmetric, so rotations about its centre leave the cloud unchanged; the registration is degenerate in those directions.

questions.prompt: You have two scans taken 40 degrees apart and no odometry. Which is the best plan?
options: Point-to-plane ICP with a huge iteration count, starting from the identity.
ICP directly from the identity pose, with enough iterations to converge.
Feature matching (e.g. FPFH) with RANSAC for a coarse pose, then ICP to refine.
Average the two clouds point by point and use the mean as the pose.
questions.explanation: Large offsets need a global method to initialise the local refinement.

questions.prompt: What does the determinant term in the 3D Kabsch solution prevent?
questions.skillLabel: Rotation from dot and cross sums
options: Noise in the correspondences from corrupting the result
A reflection being returned instead of a rotation
Scaling of the cloud being absorbed into the rotation
Translation errors from an offset between the centroids
questions.explanation: Without it the SVD can return an orthogonal matrix with determinant -1 (a mirror image).

questions.prompt: Explain in your own words why the best translation maps centroid to centroid, and what that implies for the order of the Kabsch steps.
rubric: Setting the gradient of the squared error w.r.t. t to zero gives t = mean(q) - R mean(p).
Therefore centre both clouds first, then find the rotation alone.
Mentions that skipping centring makes the rotation depend on the origin.
